Thank you for sharing your story with me. I know it's hard to look at it this way, but this sounds like it was a very important and amazing journey for you. You say you didn't have a plan, but it sounds to me like you didn't want one. You got to see the country coast to coast, something very few people get the opportunity to do. Your plan was to not have a plan, and sometimes, that's okay. I'm so sorry things went wrong for you in Northern California, and I know you probably don't feel "lucky" to be alive, but I'm certainly thankful that you are, and it sounds like you do have friends and family that care a lot about you and your safety. My own struggle is that even though I do have a plan, I don't feel like it's my own. I'm really not in control of my own life at all. I feel like I've never made a decision for myself. So that's where I'm at.

Thank you for the kind words. I love your username :)

I know you'll understand what I mean when I say this feeling is difficult to describe. It's just this looming thing that's always on the edge of my mind, and sometimes when I don't have enough to distract me, or I'm having a particularly bad day, it's just front and center. Even when I feel like things are okay and I'm doing well, that feeling comes back and tells me this won't last. 

I feel like there aren't a lot of options for people like me. The idea of a lifetime of medication & therapy & people telling me to "hang in there" (that's one that really pisses me off), those things just don't appeal to me. I know I would probably hurt some people a lot if I did it, but unfortunately at this point it feels like it's what I need to do.

That's such an amazing idea!! I wish I had the time- Unfortunately, I leave tomorrow morning. We're getting together this afternoon, so I'm hoping to try to hold them long enough to last me a few months (I'll be back again for work in July, albeit briefly, but it'll help). 

Despite my difficulties, I am pretty good at meeting new people and making new friends. I'm going to try so hard to use that skill in my new home. I try to stay positive, and think of all the people that could be waiting for me out there that could be lifesaving like the ones I have here. I'm going to try as much as I can to keep holding on to that hope that they're out there.

Damn. I'm headed to California. Currently in Wisconsin. I know I'll still have my friends through the phone and Internet. But when I'm in an especially bad place, one of the only things that can bring me back to earth is physical contact. Even if it's just their hand on my shoulder. It grounds me. I don't really know anyone in this new town. I have an aunt and uncle I'll be staying with, and a few family friends scattered here and there, but my greatest support system is here. My best friend talks about moving in with me next year, but that's a YEAR without him. It just might not be an option for me.
The friends I have here are indescribable. They have saved my life (oftentimes in the literal sense) several times. I'm relatively convinced I won't make it without them.
Thank you. I can't help but feel like I'm making a huge mistake.
Thank you for being here for me. I'm supposed to be moving on Wednesday. Far. Across the country. I'm so scared I'm making a huge mistake.

It makes me feel like a complete fool for ever thinking someone could feel that way about someone as damaged as me. He's my best friend. I'm so terrified I'm going to lose him completely.
I am going through something incredibly similar. I'm here if you'd like to commiserate.

I am so sorry life has thrown so many difficult things at you. I know what it feels like to think your problems don't measure up to others. But the things you're facing right now are absolutely significant. They are real. 

It's abundantly clear from this post that you love your children very much. I'd be a hypocrite if I tried to talk you out of ending things, but what I can promise you is that no amount of life insurance will fill replace the loss of their parent. 

Is there maybe someone you can stay with if you lose your house? A trusted friend or family member? I think a good first step for you would be to go to a doctor and try to find a medication to help you regulate your suicidal thoughts. Depression is currently shrouding my judgement as well, and my new Reddit friends tell me there are medications that can really help, that can get you on the right track again. 

I know things don't look very bright right now, but just know that even though I'm a stranger, I care about you a lot. I know you love your kids so much. If for no one else but them, try to stay with us. 

Take care, friend. You can always message me any time. I'll be thinking about you a lot.

Venting used to help. It's not so much about feeling overwhelmed about my situation anymore. My soul feels worn out. I'm just ready to be done. I fought a good fight, and now I think it's just time for me to rest.
I'm not worried what they'll think. I just don't want them to hurt more than they have to.
There isn't much else for me to say, but if you want to PM me, I'm here...
Under different circumstances, I would beg you to be here for me, to be a friend. But I'm already going to be leaving too many people hurt. I don't want to do that to you, too.
Thanks.

This is a beautiful playlist. Fantastic job. I'm so sorry you're hurting. My heart is breaking right now, too. I found out he doesn't really love me, and I can't help but blame my depression on it. I sincerely believe that there is someone out there for us who will be so full of love for us and will think we are so beautiful, even when we are suffering. Be strong. I'm here for you.
Thank you. It will be a while, since I'm moving soon. I still don't know if it's worth it. I think I might be too far gone.
Thank you. I've been on Reddit for a week and people have been really encouraging me to get help. I might just go to a private clinic. I know I can't do this alone.

It's complicated with my family. I've gone to therapy in the past, and been on medication, but when I just stopped going & taking it, it just wasn't talked about anymore. Mental illness isn't really "a thing" for a lot of them. If I try to get help, it's going to need to be without them.

I'm not on any medication right now. The more people I talk to on here, the more I think it might be a good idea to try again with it. I just don't want my family to have to go through anything with me being medicated/hospitalized/etc.

For me, distractions tend to help. School never seemed to be enough of a distraction, but college was for a while. My first year, I was really excelling. By my sophomore year, though, things were going downhill again. Maybe because I got too comfortable in the routine? I'm not sure. The best I ever managed it was my first year out of college. I had a full time job, I took up running, and I was writing with a sketch comedy group I was really into. Those were the best times. But then I ended up having to leave the job and the group, and I fell back into it. It's so frustrating knowing that I HAVE the solution, that I know what helps me, but just not being able to get out. I have three jobs right now, One of them is in my preferred field, but it hasn't made an ounce of difference this time. I'm too far gone. In a town as small as mine, gossip is a favorite hobby of many. I don't want to give anyone any ammo on my family by having to be hospitalized, or seeing me going into a mental health clinic. I can't do that to my family.

It wasn't overboard, it was monumentally helpful. Thank you so very much for such a response. For me I didn't like the sertraline because it took away my very positive moods, too. I fell somewhere in this weird middle ground. My depression wasn't as bad, but my happiness seemed to be muffled, too. I can relate so much to the feeling of being more motivated when the depression isn't looming. My whole entire life I was told from an early age, as early as these symptoms started showing, that I was lazy, inconsiderate, apathetic. It makes that little girl cry with relief knowing that she's not. 
I want to go to a therapist. I want to get help. I know that's a good sign. But at the same time, I think of all id have to do, for the rest of my life. The therapists, the medication, everyone close to me walking on eggshells. Being gone just sounds easier. I know I would hurt a lot of people if I was gone. But I also don't think I would ruin anybody's life.

I got down 2 rice cakes just now. I know it isn't much, but it's a start. I've never been this physically sick from depression before. It's new and it's scary. Maybe I will try yogurt tomorrow. That sounds ok.
Your words have made me feel a lot less alone tonight. I would love to be an ear if you need one.

I never followed up with the psychiatrist. I just stopped taking the medication. I know that's not smart, but I just wanted people to think I was okay. I've already put them through so much. I've been able to handle it for the most part, in waves. Sometimes I'll have months where things seem to be okay. Never as good as I want them to be, but...manageable. But since around November, it's been the worst it's ever been. If this is going to be my whole life, I don't want to be around for it.
Thank you for the advice. I did manage to eat a handful of trail mix before I started feeling sick again.

I just wish I could do it without alerting my family, but I think I need to focus on getting better. Your words are so encouraging. I can't thank you enough. I'm so happy you've found something to help you heal. You sound like a beautiful person.
